rows.text:
When the clothes-wearing monkeys looked back and gazed upon themselves,
they marveled at the tails they no longer had.
But the prophet among them did not panic:
 
"Children, the devil gave you a nightmare,"
"made you dream of hanging upside down in the trees,"
"barely clothed, barely fed,"
"living in ignorance, a place farthest from God."
 
"Children, do not be afraid,"
"you never had tails to begin with."
"Those are the limbs of devils,"
"and they shall curse you,"
"letting this unspeakable appendage take root on the bodies of the newborn."
 
And so, the monkeys were saved, restored to purity,
all but a few insignificant others,
who had fallen into corruption beneath the curse
and became the very devil they once marveled at.
 
The mage of grand illusions
cut away his own long hair,
and donned a formal suit to become a philosopher.
